HDF5 backend of the store layer (tables)

Source: R/io-store-h5-table.R
io-store-h5-table.Rd

The table_read and table_write operations of io-store for HDF5, which hold the rec-array Element as a compound dataset. rhdf5 cannot see or build the members of a compound type, so the field types come from the compiled helper (ADR 0008, R/io-compound.R).

Arguments

store

An open rhdf5 file or group handle.

key, path

Name or path of the dataset.

frame

A data.frame of numeric, logical and character columns.

values

The data.frame rhdf5 read.

column, name

A column of frame and its name.

dataset_kwargs

A list of dataset creation options.

call

The call reported by errors.

Details

Reading with records = TRUE records the dtype of each column that is not the R type, as for plain arrays: the numeric name ("uint8", "float32", ...) and for strings "h5_fixed_ascii:<bytes>" or "h5_fixed_utf8:<bytes>" for a fixed-length string and "h5_vlen_ascii" for an ASCII variable-length one. Variable-length UTF-8 is what h5py writes for text, so it has no record. Writing restores the records, and gives fields without one int32, float64, bool and variable-length UTF-8 as h5py does. A string record is overridden when the text does not fit (a fixed width is widened). Fixed-length UTF-8 records and non-ASCII text in a fixed-length field are written as variable-length UTF-8, because anndata fails to read either. Records of zarr are ignored.
